Earlier this summer, Apple was hit by the global memory crisis and significantly raised product prices. For example, the iPad Air went from US$599 to US$749, the MacBook Pro with M5 chip went from US$1,699 to US$1,999, and the Apple TV went from US$129 to US$199. These are just some examples — the key point is that the price hikes are quite staggering.

This situation inevitably raises the question — after the price increases, will Apple’s products see significant improvements that make them more attractive?

Of course, some Apple products are about to receive major updates, including the MacBook Pro and iPad mini. But for products that won’t see major updates anytime soon, it’s hard to imagine Apple selling outdated-spec products at much higher prices and still convincing consumers they’re worth the money — especially compared with what’s currently available on the second-hand market.

If you could buy an M4 iPad Air for US$599 (or even as low as US$499) just a few months ago, why would you be willing to pay US$749 now? The higher the price, the more glaring this issue becomes.

Some Apple products haven’t had a major refresh in a long time. The iPad Air has used the same design and features since 2020, with only chip upgrades and Apple Pencil Pro support added; the basic iPad has stayed largely the same since 2022; and the iMac hasn’t changed much since 2021.

Do these products need a redesign? Honestly, probably not. But I think Apple could take some steps to make the products more attractive at current pricing. For example, the iMac could switch to a mini-LED display, the iPad Air could add a 120Hz refresh rate, and the basic iPad could get a fully laminated display.

Compared with price hikes, these upgrades would cost very little and should help consumers more easily accept the new pricing. On the other hand, Apple may also downgrade specs on some products to offset rising costs — for example, the iPhone could once again offer a 128GB storage option.

What do you think of Apple’s product lineup after the price hikes? Feel free to share in the comments.
